description:
Follow-up to the 2026-09-13 load diagnosis (see C11-224). With ~38 terminals and one visible pane, 18 of 32 Ghostty renderer threads were doing updateFrame (rebuildRow/addGlyph) work at utility QoS: Ghostty's renderCallback rebuilds frame state for occluded surfaces and only gates drawFrame on `visible`. Every streaming agent in a hidden tab therefore keeps the 4 E-cores busy, which is what inflates load avg to 100-150 while P-cores idle.

ghostty-org fixed exactly this on 2026-05-20: 14d9e600a "renderer: skip updateFrame when surface is not visible" (14 lines in src/renderer/Thread.zig: early `if (!t.flags.visible) return .disarm;` in renderCallback, plus an updateFrame before drawFrame when the .visible mailbox message flips true). It is in ghostty-org main and in manaflow/cmux main but not in our Feb-2026 fork base. `git apply --check` fails on our base, so port it by hand.

Scope: port the commit onto Stage-11-Agentics/ghostty main (fork section 10 in docs/ghostty-fork.md, marked upstream-identical / drops out on rebase), bump the submodule pointer in c11, let build-ghosttykit pin the checksum (expect the run-1 red / run-2 action_required pattern from CLAUDE.md), then validate on a tagged build: with a background workspace streaming output, `sample` the c11 process and confirm renderer threads for occluded surfaces no longer show updateFrame/rebuildRow samples, and confirm switching to that workspace shows current content (the visibility-regain updateFrame). Ships in the next patch release together with C11-224. Fork base bump onto cmux's July base is a separate ticket.
title: Backport ghostty 14d9e600a: skip renderer updateFrame while surface is occluded
